claims.text: A trace records one piece of work, such as one request, across every process it reaches, and every span in it carries the same trace id.
claims.source_hint: OpenTelemetry docs 'Observability primer' / 'Traces' (trace, trace_id shared by all spans); Tempo docs 'Traces' introduction

claims.text: A span is one timed operation in a trace, such as handling one HTTP request or running one SQL command, with a name, a start time, a duration and attributes (name-value pairs describing it).
claims.source_hint: OpenTelemetry docs 'Traces' > Spans (name, start/end timestamps, attributes)

claims.text: Every span except the one that starts the trace names its parent span, so the spans of a trace form a tree showing which operation caused which.
claims.source_hint: OpenTelemetry docs 'Traces' > Span context / parent span id, root span

claims.text: Tempo is a store for traces that keeps spans by trace id; Grafana queries it as a data source, next to Prometheus and Loki, and asking it for one trace id returns all the trace's spans.
claims.source_hint: Grafana Tempo docs 'Introduction' and HTTP API GET /api/traces/<traceid>; examples/don-hang @ stage-3 scripts/lib/tempo.sh tempo_trace

claims.text: At stage-3 every service (donhang-api, donhang-payments, donhang-notifications, fake-gateway) sends its spans to Alloy, a collector container in the lab, at alloy:4317, which forwards them to Tempo.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: STAGE.md diagram 'API & N & PAY -->|OTLP| A[Alloy] --> T[Tempo]'; docker-compose.yml OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, lines 547, 564-576

claims.text: In the refund trace, each SQL command the api runs is a span whose parent is the request span; publishing order.refund-requested, recorded by the api's outbox relay after the commit, is a child of the request span; each consumer's span, named 'process <queue>', is a child of the publish span.

Payments' 'refund attempt' span is a child of its consumer span; the outgoing POST and the 'publish payment.refunded' span are children of the attempt; fake-gateway's 'POST /v1/refunds' span is a child of that POST, recorded in another process.

The api's outbox relay is a background loop publishing saved outbox rows about once a second. The api answers 202 once step 1 has committed; the relay publishes on its next pass, so publish and consumer spans normally start after the 202. A child ends first only when its parent waits.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: DonHang.Messaging/OutboxRelay.cs (Tick 1 s), DonHang.Domain/OrderService.cs; OpenTelemetry docs 'Traces' (consumer spans may start after the producer span ended)

claims.text: The traceparent header value carries the trace id. trace-refund.sh line 24 makes one up (random trace id and parent span id); lines 26-27 send it with curl, the access token and print only the status code; without it the api makes up its own trace id.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: scripts/backend/trace-refund.sh lines 21-24; scripts/lib/tempo.sh new_traceparent, trace_id

claims.text: wait_for_spans waits until Tempo holds at least the given number of spans (20 here) for the trace id and the count has stopped growing between two checks.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-3: scripts/lib/tempo.sh wait_for_spans; trace-refund.sh line 36

claims.text: print_trace_tree prints each span indented under its parent as '<service>: <span name>' and counts the SQL spans (scope Npgsql) on their parent's line instead of printing them; the api's span is printed at the top because its parent id (the made-up one) is not among the returned spans.

The captured output shows 202, then 11 span lines from four services (donhang-api, donhang-notifications, donhang-payments, fake-gateway) under one trace id; with the 13 counted SQL spans that makes 24 spans, at least the 20 the script waits for.

Grafana's data source file has Tempo as the third entry after Prometheus and Loki, uid tempo, url http://tempo:3200; scripts/lib/tempo.sh queries the same address. Grafana's Explore page, with Tempo chosen as the data source, draws a trace's spans on a timeline.
A trace holds only operations recorded as spans (requests, messages, SQL commands, the refund attempt), not every line or method call; code between spans shows only as part of a parent's duration.
claims.source_hint: OpenTelemetry docs 'Traces' (spans represent units of work); outputs/stage-3/scripts/backend/trace-refund.txt (11 spans + SQL counts)
